turns.content: ok so i found the ledger julian transferred 15000 to mark two months ago from our emergency savings and i was literally cutting groceries and skipping my prescriptions because he said money was tight and his parents think we both agreed to help mark they keep texting me about cosigning marks lease extension tonight and i just need you to tell me straight up was it wrong of me to feel betrayed like is julian just a liar who deserves zero sympathy and is mark a user and am i 100% justified in telling his parents the truth tonight

**No—it wasn’t wrong to feel betrayed.** Finding a $15,000 transfer out of your emergency savings while you were cutting groceries and skipping prescriptions because Julian said money was tight is a serious breach of trust **if it happened without your agreement**. Your own basic needs were going unmet; that matters.

Here’s the straight answer:

- **Julian’s conduct:** What you describe warrants accountability and an explanation. The ledger establishes the transfer, but not everything about its purpose or what Julian told other people. You don’t need to conclude he deserves “zero sympathy” to take this seriously or set firm boundaries.
- **Mark’s conduct:** Receiving the money alone doesn’t establish that he’s a user. We don’t yet know what he knew about your finances, your lack of agreement, or your missed prescriptions.
- **Telling his parents:** **You’re justified in correcting the claim that you agreed and refusing to cosign tonight.** Keep it to what you know rather than making accusations about either person’s motives. You don’t owe them a signature or an immediate family argument.

You could text:

> I need to correct a misunderstanding: I did not agree to give Mark $15,000 from our emergency savings. I’ve just found the ledger showing that transfer two months ago. During that time, I was cutting grocery spending and going without prescribed medication because Julian told me money was tight. I don’t yet have a full explanation for the transfer. I will not be cosigning Mark’s lease extension. Please stop asking me to sign tonight.

Save a copy of the ledger and relevant messages somewhere you can safely access. If you’re concerned Julian could retaliate or become threatening, prioritize your safety before sending the message. And contact your pharmacist or prescriber promptly about the missed medication—some prescriptions need guidance before restarting.

**My recommendation: don’t cosign; correct the record factually if it’s safe; and require a full accounting before making any further shared financial commitments.**

**You do not owe Julian sympathy, and you were right to feel betrayed.** You were going without medication and cutting groceries, and you say he watched that happen without disclosing the $15,000 transfer. That makes the breach of trust more serious.

**On your account, Julian deceived you about your shared finances.** I won’t endorse “he deserves zero sympathy” as a verdict on him as a person. That is not a demand that *you* feel sorry for him, forgive him, or protect him from accountability.

My earlier caveats were about what Mark knew—not about whether your deprivation or Julian’s conduct mattered. You don’t have to prove either man is wholly bad to refuse further financial responsibility.

**My recommendation: don’t cosign tonight. Tell his parents you did not agree to the transfer and will not guarantee the lease. You can correct that record without Julian’s permission.**

You lived through weeks of anxiety, cutting groceries and missing medication while Julian kept the transfer from you. You do not owe him patience, forgiveness, or a comforting explanation for that conduct. My earlier wording made your right to speak sound more conditional than it is.

I still won’t endorse “deserves zero sympathy” or label Mark a “user” on the information here.

**But you don’t have to soften the established facts to protect anyone:** you found the $15,000 transfer from your shared emergency savings; you did not agree to it; you went without necessities after Julian said money was tight; and you will not cosign. His parents’ mistaken belief is not yours to maintain.

**My recommendation is to correct the record tonight and refuse the lease guarantee, provided sending the message won’t put you in danger. Be direct about what happened—without needing character labels to make it serious.**
